exl3.d: ExLlamaV3's weight quantization format, described as a streamlined variant of QTIP: randomized Hadamard rotation (suh/svh), a bitshift trellis with a 16-bit state and a computed codebook (MCG, mul1 or 3INST), in 16×16 tiles with an integer number \(k\) of bits per weight. The recipe's GLM-5.3-Flash experts use EXL3 K4 with MCG.

fator-de-crista.d: The ratio between the largest absolute value in a group and its RMS, \(\kappa = a_{\max}/\sigma\). The relative error of a uniform quantization scaled by the maximum grows with \(\kappa^2\); it is the number that Hadamard rotations knock down.

incoerencia.d: The property of a matrix with no standout elements: a small \(\mu(W) = \max|W_{ij}|\sqrt{mn}/\|W\|_F\). Incoherence processing (QuIP, QuIP#, QTIP, EXL3) rotates the matrix with orthogonal transforms to make it incoherent before quantizing.

transformada-hadamard.d: Multiplication by an orthogonal matrix with entries \(\pm 1/\sqrt n\), built recursively (Sylvester): \(H_{2n} = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}[[H_n, H_n],[H_n, -H_n]]\). It is symmetric and its own inverse (\(HH = I\)), and it mixes each coordinate with all the others.

fwht.d: An algorithm that applies \(H_n\) in \(\log_2 n\) stages of butterflies \((a, b) \to (a+b, a-b)\): \(n\log_2 n\) additions and no multiplications, except for the final \(1/\sqrt n\) factor. In EXL3, \(n = 128\): 2 stages inside each thread and 5 via __shfl_xor_sync.

hadamard-randomizado.d: A Hadamard preceded by a diagonal of random signs \(S = \mathrm{diag}(\pm1)\): \(HS\) is still orthogonal and fast, and with high probability it doesn't line up with any structure in the weights. It is the rotation used by QuIP#, QTIP and EXL3.

suh-svh.d: The two FP16 vectors of each EXL3 matrix: suh (size \(d_{\text{in}}\)) multiplies the activation before the input Hadamard, and svh (size \(d_{\text{out}}\)) multiplies the output after the output Hadamard: \(W = \mathrm{diag}(suh)\,H\,\hat W\,H\,\mathrm{diag}(svh)\). They carry signs and magnitudes; there is no per-block scale.

quantizacao-vetorial.d: Quantizing \(d\) values at once, replacing the vector with its nearest neighbor in a codebook of \(2^{kd}\) vectors. It beats scalar quantization in space filling and in shape, but the codebook grows exponentially with \(d\).

codebook.d: The set of values (or vectors) a quantizer can reconstruct: the stored code is the index, and the decoder returns the corresponding entry. It can be an explicit table or a function computed from the index.

qtip.d: Quantization with Trellises and Incoherence Processing (Tseng, Sun, Hou and De Sa, NeurIPS 2024): LLM weight quantization with randomized Hadamard + bitshift trellis + computed codebooks (1MAD, 3INST, HYB), which behaves like a 256-dimensional VQ with cheap decoding. It is the basis of EXL3.

tcq.d: Quantization in which the decoder is a state machine: each weight consumes \(K\) bits, but its value depends on an \(L\)-bit state formed by the most recent bits. Optimal encoding is a shortest path through the trellis (Viterbi).

trelica-bitshift.d: A trellis whose state is a sliding window over the bit stream: \(s_t = ((s_{t-1} \ll K)\,|\,b_t) \bmod 2^L\), and \(\hat w_t = c(s_t)\). Neighboring weights share \(L-K\) bits. In EXL3, \(L = 16\) and \(K\) = bits per weight.

viterbi.d: Dynamic programming that finds the lowest-cost path through a trellis: \(J_t(s) = \min_{s'\to s} J_{t-1}(s') + \text{cost}(s)\), storing the best predecessor of each state and retracing the path backward. It costs \(O(T\cdot 2^L\cdot 2^K)\): expensive, but done once, offline.

tail-biting.d: A circular trellis: the state of the first step is formed by the last symbols of the block, so there are no initialization bits. In EXL3, each weight's 16-bit window is read modulo the tile size (256·K bits).

codebook-computado.d: A codebook with no table: the value is computed from the state with a few integer instructions (multiply, mask/XOR, byte sum), producing an approximately Gaussian distribution. It avoids storing and looking up 65,536 entries in every thread.

mcg.d: EXL3 codebook cb=1: \(x = s\cdot\mathtt{0xCBAC1FED} \bmod 2^{32}\), \(y = (x\,\&\,\mathtt{0x8FFF8FFF})\oplus\mathtt{0x3B603B60}\), value = the sum of the two halves of \(y\) read as FP16 (σ ≈ 1.244). int32 marker −877912083. Used in the GLM experts.

mul1.d: EXL3 codebook cb=2: \(x = s\cdot\mathtt{0x83DCD12D}\), the sum of the 4 bytes via dp4a added to 0x6400 (FP16 1024) and normalized by an FMA \(\times\) 0x1EEE (≈ 1/147.8) \(+\) 0xC931 (= −10.383), which gives ≈ N(0,1) by the Central Limit Theorem. Marker −2082680531. Used in turboderp's EXL3 dense layers.

lop3.d: A PTX instruction that computes any logic function of three 32-bit inputs, selected by an 8-bit truth table. MCG uses lop3.b32 x, x, 0x8fff8fff, 0x3b603b60, 0x6a, that is, \((x\,\&\,m) \oplus c\) in a single instruction.

dp4a.d: A GPU instruction that computes the dot product of two 4-byte vectors and adds it to a 32-bit accumulator. With the vector 0x01010101, it sums the 4 bytes of a word; the mul1 codebook uses it because it is native on Blackwell (the older vabsdiff4 is emulated).

marcador-codebook.d: An int32 [1] tensor stored alongside each EXL3 matrix (mcg or mul1) holding the codebook multiplier reinterpreted as signed. The loader checks the value and refuses the checkpoint (“packed ABI mismatch”) if it isn't the codebook the kernel implements.

uniform-k4.d: A quantization policy in which every tensor in scope gets the same \(k = 4\) bits per weight, with no sensitivity-based allocation. It is the policy of GLM's TR3 checkpoint (tensor_policy uniform-routed-experts, global_allocator_invoked false); fractional rates like “4.05bpw” are allocations of different integer \(k\) values across tensors.

precisao-por-shard.d: In a fused projection (e.g. QKV), each output shard can have a different format. In GLM's dense-EXL3 pack, non_routed_exl3.layers declares bits and bf16_shards (the contiguous tail that stays in BF16, such as the drafter's K/V).

sentinela-k16.d: A bits-per-weight value that the ExLlamaV3 converter interprets as “don't quantize”: the tensor stays in BF16. The GLM recipe uses K = 16 for the 6 bpw drafter's k_proj/v_proj and head_bits = 16 to keep the lm_head native.

registrador.d: Each GPU thread's private memory, the fastest of all, read at the pace of the instruction itself. The SM has a register file split among the resident threads; that is where the EXL3 kernels decode each weight to FP16, without writing the matrix anywhere.

conflito-de-banco.d: Shared memory is divided into 32 banks of 4 bytes, and each bank serves one address per cycle. When threads of the same warp request different addresses in the same bank, the accesses are serialized. Random lookups into a table (such as a 65,536-entry codebook) hit this case all the time.

iq2-xxs.d: A 2.0625-bit-per-weight format from ggml (llama.cpp), in groups of 256, that stores indices into a fixed grid of values (a codebook). Used for the experts of Nemotron-3.5-Bolt's 24 GB pack; it needs custom kernels.

largura-mista.d: Giving each tensor, or group of tensors, its own number of bits according to its sensitivity and the bytes it reads per step: for example, experts at 2–3 bits, attention at 5, head at 6, selectors in BF16. It's what the EXL3 “EAQ” packs and ModelOpt's mixed-precision recipes do.
